title: implement 2D max pooling

atoms.evidence: oh = 1 + (h - kh) // stride_h; ow = 1 + (w - kw) // stride_w — same formula as conv, just applied to maxpool
x_strided = x_padded.as_strided(size=(b, ic, oh, ow, kh, kw), stride=(s_b, s_c, s_h * stride_h, s_w * stride_w, s_h, s_w)) — identical structure to conv2d
return x_strided.amax(dim=(-1, -2)) — max-reduce over the two kernel dims; exercise explicitly contrasts with conv: 'simply taking max over those dimensions rather than a dot product with the kernel'
x_padded = pad2d(x, ..., pad_value=-t.inf) — KEY teaching point in dropdown: pad with -inf (not 0) so padded cells lose the max; same padding mechanism, different fill value
stride scales the output-position dim strides in as_strided; default stride=kernel_size for maxpool (vs default stride=1 for conv)

atoms_in_seed_but_not_actually_present.reason: this is the plain function maxpool2d (not a MaxPool2d nn.Module); the Module wrapper is composed into ResNet34 in 0_2_9 but never explicitly defined as an exercise

notes: 6-atom exercise — heavy reuse of the conv2d skeleton with the kernel-multiplication swapped for an amax reduction. Validates that maxpool-reduce belongs in the convolution-windowing-and-aggregation family (same windowing primitive, different aggregator). The pad_value=-t.inf trick is a memorable cross-atom interaction (conv-padding-zero + maxpool-reduce) — possibly worth a future 'padding-and-reduction-compatibility' atom if other reductions show similar issues.
